messages:
Anna (SecOps): EDR alert: Ben's MacBook triggered 'UntrustedProcess' rule. Binary /tmp/.upd_x flagged, spawned `curl https://45.77.81.90/ping` and created TLS session. I quarantined the file and isolated the device from the network. Please advise next steps. :eyes:
EDR Bot: Detection ID det-8942, score 0.87. File hash sha256: abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890. Child processes: curl (pid 7182). Network: 45.77.81.90:443. Dropped file to /var/tmp/edr_artifacts/det-8942.tar.gz
Mike (Oncall): Thanks. Anna — did the user have any vault or KMS access active? Any SSH keys on disk? :thinking:
Anna (SecOps): Ben had standard dev role, no org-wide KMS keys. But he does have access to project-kms via gcloud auth. I'm pulling access logs now.
Jordan (IT): I'll confirm whether device had any persistent VPN sessions or mounted network drives. Ben — were you running any 3rd-party updaters just now?
Ben (Eng): I clicked an app update prompt for 'FastSync' ~10m ago. It's a 3rd-party app we use for local syncing. Thought it was legit. :grimacing:
Anna (SecOps): Good to know. Please don't power off the machine yet. We need a full triage run. Can you open Terminal and run `edrctl collect --det det-8942 --output /tmp/collect.tgz` and upload to the incident bucket? I'll provide presigned URL.
Ben (Eng): Running now.
EDR Bot: Collection complete: /var/tmp/edr_artifacts/collect-det-8942.tgz (12MB). Upload link: https://s3.redwood.internal/incident-uploads/collect-det-8942.tgz
Anna (SecOps): Downloaded. Quick grep: no evidence of ~/.ssh/authorized_keys modifications, no new API tokens in shell history. Running YARA scan locally and starting memory dump.
Mike (Oncall): Also check Cloud KMS logs: who used project-kms keys in last 2 hours. If any access from Ben's machine IP, escalate.
Jordan (IT): On it. Also adding temporary host firewall rule to block 45.77.81.90 at edge.
Anna (SecOps): YARA found a small packer stub but no obvious exfil module. Memory dump shows an in-memory curl session but no large uploads. Preliminary judgement: likely a malicious updater that phoned home for commands, not straightforward data exfil. More thorough scan next.
Ben (Eng): Do I need to reimage? I can reprovision if that's the call.
Mike (Oncall): Let's hold. If no credentials or secrets used and we can remove persistence, we can avoid reimaging immediately. Ops: prepare reimage plan in case. :lock:
Anna (SecOps): Action items: 1) Jordan to block IP and add IDS rule for 45.77.81.90, 2) Mike to check KMS/console audit for any anomalous key use, 3) Ben to provide installed package list and any consented external installers, 4) Anna to write YARA/EDR rule and coordinate reimaging if persistence found. We'll reconvene in 30m. :white_check_mark:
Jordan (IT): Blocked IP at perimeter and created firewall ticket FW-1182. Added IDS rule signature temp-block.
Mike (Oncall): KMS logs: no key usage from Ben's device or his account in last 24h. No suspicious console sessions.
Anna (SecOps): Good. Final: no evidence of secret theft. We've kept the device isolated, quarantined the file, and scheduled a follow-up scan and optional reimage. Filing incident report and tagging for post-incident review (PI-2023-47). If anything changes, update thread.
Ben (Eng): Thanks team. Will avoid FastSync until we confirm.
Anna (SecOps): Closing initial triage. Follow-up tasks: update onboarding docs to warn about unsigned updaters, add process whitelist check to endpoint policy. :memo:
